info.title: network-monitor — read-only API
info.summary: The reachability history the page shows, as JSON
info.description: Read-only and unauthenticated, served on the socket the page already binds: it never writes and it never needs a credential. Every success is an object whose `data` holds an array and whose `meta` echoes the request; every failure is an object with a stable `code` and a fixed `message`. The data routes stream: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, no `Content-Length`, gzip on the fly when the client accepts it. A breaking change means a new `/api/vN` prefix.

get.summary: Faults, down time, and up runs per UTC day, oldest first
get.description: The window is the last 30 days when the request names none, and it may be as wide as the accepted domain allows (47 482 days at most): only the days the page returns are read, so the cost follows `limit`, not the span. A day that the window clips at its edges counts only what falls inside it; a day that has not begun yet states no faults, no down time and no up run, because unelapsed time is not measured; and the UTC day still running is flagged `partial`: its average and longest up run cover the last 24 hours, like the detail page.

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API

Target.name: target
Target.description: Canonical key (`icmp://1.1.1.1`) or the label of a target. An unknown value answers `404 UNKNOWN_TARGET`.

From.name: from
From.description: Start of the window, inclusive: an RFC 3339 UTC instant such as `2026-11-14T22:00:00.000Z`, or epoch milliseconds. An instant lies between `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z` and `2100-01-01T00:00:00Z`, both accepted; a value outside answers `400 INVALID_PARAMETER`.

To.name: to
To.description: End of the window, exclusive, in the same two forms and inside the same calendar domain as `from`. It must be later than `from`, and it may be in the future, so a whole month or year can be asked for; the days after today state no faults and no down time.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: How many records the page holds.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: How many records to skip. Paging a list that grows at the top can repeat a record; use `from`/`to` for a stable window.

BadRequest.description: A parameter the route does not accept, a value out of range, or a window that ends before it starts

UnknownTarget.description: The `target` filter names no target in the database

Unavailable.description: The database is missing or was never opened by this tool

total.description: How many records match the filters, whatever the page holds

target.description: The canonical key the filter resolved to, or null

from.description: The start actually applied, defaults included

to.description: The end actually applied, defaults included

target.description: The canonical key of the target

label.description: The label of the target, or null

interface.description: The interface the probe is bound to, or null for the default route

stateSinceMs.description: The same instant in epoch milliseconds

lastRttUs.description: The round-trip time of the last successful probe, in microseconds

upForMs.description: How long the target has been up without a drop; null while it is not up

Fault.description: One fault: the `down` transition that opened it, its cause, and the return that closed it. A fault always opens on a `down` event, so no `state` and no round-trip time are stated: both would be constants.

cause.description: The code of the failure, such as ICMP.NO_REPLY

causeMessage.description: The standard message of that cause, as it was rendered

endedAt.description: The instant the target came back; null while it is still down

durationMs.description: How long the fault lasted; null while it is still open

ongoing.description: True while the target is still down

target.description: The canonical key of the target when the request filters by one; null when the record aggregates every target

faults.description: Faults that started inside the day and the window

downMs.description: Time spent down inside the day, clipped to the window

avgUpRunMs.description: Mean of the up runs inside the day; null when the day holds none

longestUpRunMs.description: The longest up run inside the day

partial.description: True for the UTC day still running: its runs cover the last 24 hours

status.description: The HTTP status of the answer

parameter.description: The query parameter the answer is about, when there is one
